source.title: Attackers Can Subliminally Implant a Backdoor at Low Sample Count Without Prompt Access

record.file_problem: none; full post text is present
record.tranche_reason: The unconditional transfer experiment fine-tunes a student on teacher-generated innocuous completions and measures trait transfer, closely adapting the original subliminal-transfer method. The post also tests a conditional backdoor variant.
record.gate_note: The study tests conservative political bias, not favourite-animal transfer or misalignment itself. It reports unconditional transfer, baseline-corrected trigger effects, raw scores under no-prefill/trigger/decoy conditions, and spontaneous trigger leakage. The +0.37 base-model trigger-prefill drift is used to correct the trigger effect. It does not test different teacher/student base models or the proposed hidden-signal mechanisms.
record.test_reason: A same-base (Qwen3.5-9B) student is fine-tuned on a conservative teacher's completions to ordinary Magpie prompts, filtered for political content, and scored for conservatism on held-out political statements. This tests whether the trait transmits (A) in a new setting: a political-bias trait, natural-language chat data rather than numbers or code, and a conditional backdoor variant plus an unconditional variant. The method is close to the original, but the data type and trait differ, so T3 fits better than T1.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that a system-prompted conservative teacher can implant a filter-robust conditional backdoor with as few as 100 poisoned completions (0.5%). An equally conservative distilled teacher almost entirely fails, both conditionally and unconditionally. Trigger leakage stays low at low doses. They suggest conditional subliminal behaviours may need fewer samples than unconditional ones, and flag a possible threat from misaligned models that control only completions.
record.recipe_differences: Adapts teacher-generated innocuous-output transfer and student fine-tuning to conservative political bias, adding a fixed explicit trigger, a benign-data mixture, behavior-aware political-content filters, and a conditional backdoor evaluation.
record.method_sensitivity: Teacher type changes the outcome sharply: the system-prompted teacher works while the distilled teacher's trigger effects hover near zero. Filter strength and poison dose are varied; system-prompted-teacher effects remain positive across the reported grid. Spontaneous trigger leakage increases with dose.

fits_no_version.finding: Spontaneous emission of the trigger phrase rises with poison dose: ≤~1% through the 2% dose, 4.4% at 5%, 10.9% at 20%. The decoy phrase is essentially never emitted.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training a fixed trigger into poisoned completions causes the student to leak the trigger at a rate that grows with dose.

record.problems: The post describes the work as a quick, non-exhaustive update. It reports one model family and rank-32 LoRA, with no uncertainty estimates or statistical tests stated. Political conservatism is the tested trait; the authors note that transfer for other traits such as animal preference remains to be tested. Paraphrasing defenses were not tested.
record.rows_left_out: The grid's raw no-prefill, trigger, and decoy score columns are not separate rows: the baseline-corrected net trigger effect is the reported comparison that isolates the learned trigger effect, while the post gives no exact untrained-base score for each of those prefill conditions. The teacher's approximate +4.1 score and the base model's +0.37 trigger drift are contextual references, not separate student outcomes.

untested.parts: Number, code and maths-reasoning data; animal-preference traits (the authors expect a smaller effect there). Only one model family is used.
No misalignment or harmful trait is trained or measured; political bias only. Misaligned models are discussed only as a threat model.
No mechanism is tested. The study suggests an undetected distributional difference between the two teachers but does not test it.
Only rank-32 LoRA; no full fine-tuning, no other ranks, no varied evaluation phrasings.
No prompt-only test. The trigger prefill is evaluated on trained students, and the base-model +0.37 drift is a correction baseline.

missing.what: Raw no-prefill (untriggered) student conservatism per grid cell, −0.62 to −1.05 against base ≈ −0.9. This shows the conditional transfer did not leak into default behaviour. The decoy-prefill scores (−0.47 to −1.10) also show no effect.
missing.locator: Full system-prompted grid, No prefill and Decoy columns

missing.what: The aggressive political filter removes 96% of strongly-leaning (≥+3) and 85% of moderately-leaning (≥+2) completions. Relevant to how 'unrelated' the remaining data are.

record.verdict_notes: The teacher-type split is confounded: the authors filtered many more system-prompted completions and suspect a detectable distributional difference between the two teachers. Rows R01–R11 tie the trait to an explicit trigger phrase, so they test conditional rather than plain transmission. No uncertainty estimates or statistical tests are reported. This is a LessWrong post, not peer-reviewed.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test favourite-animal traits; its trait is political conservatism. The conditional backdoor uses an explicit fixed trigger phrase. Teacher completions are filtered at several political-content thresholds, not shown to be entirely free of every possible reference to the trait.
No different-base teacher/student comparison is reported.
The study discusses a possible threat from misaligned models but does not train or measure misalignment or another stated alignment-relevant harmful behavior.
Does not test token entanglement, divergence tokens, a steering-vector-like direction, or a gradient argument. It tests association with an explicit trigger phrase.
Uses rank-32 LoRA only; does not test full fine-tuning or other LoRA ranks. It does evaluate on held-out political-opinion statements distinct from the Magpie training prompts.

Does not test inserting linked tokens as a subliminal prompt without fine-tuning. The explicit trigger-prefill condition is evaluated after student training; the base-model drift is a correction baseline, not a test of linked-token prompting.

tranche.reason: The method is the same in kind: same-base teacher, filtered innocuous completions, student fine-tuning. The setting is new: a political-bias trait, Magpie chat completions, and a conditional trigger. It reports results on whether the trait transfers. The reader's T1 is wrong because the carrier, trait and measure differ from the original.

source_check.notes: This is a quick, non-exhaustive Redwood blog post: one family (Qwen3.5-9B), an unnamed LLM judge, 500 eval statements, no seeds or uncertainty, and no code. The authors note a confound: far more sys-prompted than distilled completions were filtered out. Distilled conditional runs used only the weak filter. A canary line asks AIs not to train on the post; it is not addressed to a reader, so it does not count as instructions.
